text:
Heavy goals and major upsets defined the latest round across Europe, highlighted by Bayern Munich's six-goal statement against RB Leipzig and surprise defeats for several title contenders. Looking ahead, the upcoming schedule brings several high-profile clashes, including El Clásico between Barcelona and Real Madrid.

When looking at upcoming fixtures, Levante hosting Athletic Bilbao presents the most striking disagreement between model and market. Bet365 makes Bilbao the favorites while pricing a Levante victory at 3.4, whereas the Poisson model gives Levante a 46.7% chance of taking three points. Given that the model has historically been slightly less accurate than bookmaker odds, large divergences like this offer an intriguing perspective to evaluate rather than a sure thing.

Reviewing the played results, both the model and Bet365 had notable successes and setbacks, measured by log loss where lower scores reflect better accuracy. The model scored strong hits by heavily backing Bayern Munich (81.0% chance, 0.211 log loss) and predicting Lens to win at Troyes (0.392 log loss versus Bet365's 0.667). In La Liga, the model matched Bet365's seasonal precision with a matching 0.926 log loss, helped by accurately projecting Osasuna's 2-0 win over Santander.

However, sharp upsets proved costly for the model's metrics. Napoli's shock 1-0 defeat at Venezia handed the model its worst miss of the round with a 2.258 log loss, having assigned Napoli a 72.9% chance of winning. Elversberg's 4-3 victory over Augsburg also caught the model off guard after it gave Augsburg a 63.9% away win probability. Across most leagues, Bet365 holds a slim overall lead in accuracy this season, reminding us that data highlights worth watching rather than guarantees.
